claims.claim: In a cross-sectional comparison, 39 percent of GLP-1 users reported nail detachment versus 9 percent of controls.
claims.episode_span: Nail detachment was reported by 39 percent of users and 9 percent of controls
claims.source_title: GLP-1 Drugs Linked to Nail and Hair Problems
claims.supporting_quote: Nail detachment, in which the nail separates from the underlying nail bed, was reported by 39% of GLP-1 users, compared with 9% of controls.

claims.claim: The nail and hair comparison included 575 GLP-1 users and 1,329 never-users with obesity and/or type 2 diabetes from France, the US, Brazil, and Mexico.
claims.episode_span: 575 people using GLP-1 receptor agonists and 1,329 people with obesity and/or type 2 diabetes
claims.source_title: GLP-1 Drugs Linked to Nail and Hair Problems
claims.supporting_quote: The study compared 575 people using GLP-1 medications with 1,329 individuals with obesity and/or type 2 diabetes who had never taken the drugs. Participants were recruited from France, the US, Brazil, and Mexico.

claims.claim: Nail discoloration was reported by 46 percent of GLP-1 users versus 17 percent of nonusers, and 66 percent of users reported at least one nail disorder versus 53 percent of controls.
claims.episode_span: nail discoloration by 46 percent versus 17 percent, and at least one nail disorder by 66 percent versus 53 percent
claims.source_title: GLP-1 Drugs Linked to Nail and Hair Problems
claims.supporting_quote: Nail discoloration was also more common among users, affecting 46% versus 17% of nonusers. Overall, 66% of users reported at least one nail disorder, compared with 53% of controls.

claims.claim: After accounting for dermatological conditions and nutritional deficiencies, nail detachment and discoloration remained about two to three times more frequent among GLP-1 users.
claims.episode_span: Detachment and discoloration stayed about two to three times as common
claims.source_title: GLP-1 Drugs Linked to Nail and Hair Problems
claims.supporting_quote: After accounting for dermatological conditions and nutritional deficiencies, nail detachment and discoloration remained approximately two to three times more frequent among users.

claims.claim: Unusual hair loss was reported by 50 percent of GLP-1 users versus 34 percent of controls, reduced hair density by 42 versus 19 percent, and scalp redness was about three times as common among users.
claims.episode_span: unusual hair loss was 50 percent versus 34 percent, reduced hair volume or density 42 percent versus 19 percent
claims.source_title: GLP-1 Drugs Linked to Nail and Hair Problems
claims.supporting_quote: Unusual hair loss was reported by 50% of GLP-1 users, compared with 34% of controls, while reduced hair volume or density affected 42% versus 19%.

claims.claim: A surgical-record analysis of 2,028,601 patients, including 145,610 taking GLP-1 medications, found 11 percent lower odds of major cardiovascular complications and 8 percent lower odds of postoperative infections among users after matching.
claims.episode_span: users had 11 percent lower odds of major cardiovascular complications and 8 percent lower odds of postoperative infections.
claims.source_title: GLP-1 Drugs Linked to Fewer Heart Complications and Infections After Surgery, New Study Finds
claims.supporting_quote: After matching users with similar nonusers, the team found 11% lower odds of major cardiovascular complications and 8% lower odds of postoperative infections among people taking the drugs.

claims.claim: In the tighter surgical comparison, major cardiovascular complications occurred in 1.0 percent of GLP-1 users versus 1.1 percent of nonusers, and postoperative infections in 4.9 percent versus 5.3 percent.

claims.supporting_quote: In that comparison, major cardiovascular complications occurred in 1.0% of GLP-1 users versus 1.1% of nonusers. Postoperative infections affected 4.9% and 5.3%, respectively.

claims.claim: The Partnership for Safe Medicines filed a citizen petition on October 16 asking the FDA to block compounding of BPC-157, KPV, TB-500, MOTS-c, emideltide, semax, and epitalon.
claims.episode_span: On October 16 the Partnership for Safe Medicines filed a citizen petition
claims.source_title: PSM files Citizen Petition with FDA to stop unsafe compounding of untested peptides
claims.supporting_quote: On Friday October 16th, the Partnership for Safe Medicines filed a citizen petition (CP) with the FDA asking them to refrain from taking action, whether through regulation, addition to “Category 1” of the Interim Bulk Compounding policy, or exercise of enforcement discretion to allow for compounding of drug products using seven peptide bulk drug substances (BPC-157, KPV, TB-500, MOTS-c, emideltide, semax, and epitalon).

claims.claim: FDA scientists recommended against bulk compounding of seven peptides, and the Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee voted to allow six of the seven.
claims.episode_span: Agency scientists had recommended against bulk compounding of all seven; the committee voted to allow six of the seven
claims.source_title: Partnership for Safe Medicines Files Citizen Petition Urging FDA to Block Compounding of Unapproved and Uncharacterized Peptides
claims.supporting_quote: At a Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee (PCAC) meeting convened by the FDA in July, the agency’s scientists recommended against bulk compounding of seven substances under consideration – BPC-157, KPV, TB-500, MOTS-c, emideltide, semax, and epitalon. The Committee, whose newly appointed members include individuals with financial ties to the peptide industry , voted in favor of allowing six out of the seven unapproved substances to be compounded.
